originality.rationale: The claim is the exact initial-state-dependent constrained optimal directional colonization allocation in a continuous-time two-patch chain, not the classical finite Markov absorption method. Inspected Day–Possingham (1995) covers discrete-time transition matrices; Ross–Pollett (2009) optimizes homogeneous rates and explicitly leaves patch targeting as future study. A closely related 2001 conservation paper was accessible only at abstract level, so historical priority is provisional, not asserted with certainty.
residual_risks: The exact contents of Etienne–Heesterbeek (2001), directly relevant to intervention allocation, could not be read in full and may contain an equivalent special case.
A more general conservation-control theorem or an inaccessible full-text appendix might imply the projector formula.
The cited discrete-time predecessors and the present continuous-time model must not be conflated; priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: Mean global-extinction time is a standard conservation objective and allocating limited, direction-specific corridors is a natural resource problem. The exact optimizer gives a genuine interior-vs-one-way policy boundary driven by initial occupancy and local hazard, and shows the counterintuitive universal equal split from full occupancy despite unequal extinction rates. Unlike a numerical case, it classifies all initial distributions and feasible baseline intervals, with an exact misallocation penalty; it is not claimed for other ecological objectives.
